subject.title: feat(llama-cpp): in-process local GGUF text inference provider

question: Should OpenClaw endorse an externally installed in-process llama.cpp runtime and this specific 2.5 GB community-hosted GGUF as the universal zero-key onboarding fallback?
rationale: The choice establishes first-run provider ranking, download and hardware expectations, artifact trust policy, and an endorsed default model; implementation correctness cannot settle those product decisions.

options.title: Adopt after hardening
options.body: Keep the plugin-owned design, but require immutable artifact integrity and cross-platform fresh-install and agent-turn proof before enabling it broadly.

options.title: Ship explicit provider only
options.body: Expose text inference to users who deliberately install and configure the plugin while deferring the universal onboarding option and default download.

options.title: Defer local fallback
options.body: Continue relying on existing local-runtime and custom llama.cpp-server routes until maintainers settle the zero-key onboarding strategy.

recommendation.title: Adopt after hardening
recommendation.body: Keep the plugin-owned design, but require immutable artifact integrity and cross-platform fresh-install and agent-turn proof before enabling it broadly.

likelyOwner.reason: This contributor has the strongest merged-history connection to the llama.cpp plugin ownership boundary affected by the decision.
